QF.id: AIFM CIII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_7

question.text: Mr. Ramesh Iyer invested INR 5 crore in Sahyadri Stat-Arb Fund on 01-Jan. The PPM specifies a 2% exit load on the gross redemption value (NAV x units) if redeemed within 12 months. He redeems on 01-Aug the same year when the gross exit value at NAV is INR 6 crore. What is the net proceed after the exit load, ignoring taxes?

answer.text: INR 6.00 crore — exit load applies only to capital, not gains
INR 5.88 crore — 2% load on gross exit value of INR 6 cr
INR 5.90 crore — 2% load applied on INR 5 cr invested principal
INR 4.90 crore — 2% on invested capital plus profit clawback

explanation.text: The Logic: The stem fixes the exit-load convention in the PPM as 2% of the gross redemption value (NAV x units). The applicable load = 2% x INR 6 cr = INR 12 lakh; net proceeds = INR 6 cr - INR 12 lakh = INR 5.88 cr. The Trap: Option A misreads the PPM by exempting gains from the load. Option C loads on invested principal rather than the PPM-defined gross redemption value. Option D invents a profit clawback that is not part of the stated PPM rule. Note: Exit load is a charge levied at the time of redemption, expressed in the PPM as a percentage of NAV / gross redemption value (workbook pp. 112 and 125). The exact base (gross NAV vs invested capital) must be read from the PPM.
